인간의 잘 믿는 성향에 관한 논의는 흔히 아이들을 그리지만. <break time="0.8s" /> 매우 잘 속는 존재로. <break time="0.8s" /> 실험들은 어린아이들이 이미 정교한 방법을 사용한다는 것을 보여 준다. <break time="0.8s" /> 즉 누구를 믿을지 결정하기 위한 방법 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그런 실험들 중 일부에서, 아이들은 두 사람과 상호작용한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 두 사람은 이전에 낯설었던 물건에 서로 다른 이름을 붙인다. <break time="0.8s" /> 아이는 누구를 믿을지 결정해야 한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 일반적으로, 어린 나이부터 아이들은 믿는 쪽을 택하곤 한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 자신과 강한 관계를 맺고 있는 사람을 낯선 사람보다. <break time="0.8s" /> 세 살 때는, 그들은 여전히 이렇게 할 것이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 설령 친숙한 사람이 전력이 있더라도. <break time="0.8s" /> 즉 물건에 이름들을 붙인 전력 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그 이름들은 아이가 틀렸다고 알아차린 것이었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 다섯 살이 되면, 그들은 더 많은 신뢰를 보낼 것이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 정확했던 전력이 어느 정도 있는 비교적 낯선 사람에게. <break time="0.8s" /> 부정확한 기록이 있는 친숙한 사람에게보다. <break time="0.8s" /> 둘 중에서 골라야 할 두 낯선 사람이 있다면 어떻게 될까 두 사람 다 비슷한 정확도 기록을 가진 경우에 말이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그러면 낯선 사람 중에서 다음 출신인 사람이 즉 아이와 같은 문화 집단 출신인 사람이. <break time="0.8s" /> 예를 들어 억양으로 판단해서. <break time="0.8s" /> 믿음을 받는 사람이 된다. <break time="0.8s" /> 실험은 어른들을 대상으로도 행해져 왔는데. <break time="0.8s" /> 그들은 아이들과 마찬가지로 이론의 출처에 관한 정보를 사용한다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그것을 받아들일지 여부를 결정하기 위해. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리는 여론 주도자와 권위 있는 사람들을 따르는 경향이 있다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 우리와 신념을 공유하는 사람들을. <break time="0.8s" /> 비슷한 실험들은 침팬지들 사이에서 다음을 보여 준다. <break time="0.8s" /> 더 높은 지위를 가진 개체들이 더 많이 신뢰받는다는 것을. <break time="0.8s" /> 우리 모두는 누구를 믿을지 결정하는 방법이 필요하다. <break time="0.8s" /> 진화는 우리와 다른 종들에게 출발점을 제공해 주었다.

While discussions of human credulity often portray children as being highly credulous, experiments show that young children already use sophisticated methods for deciding whom to trust. <break time="0.8s" /> In some such experiments, children interact with two individuals who give different names to previously unfamiliar objects. <break time="0.8s" /> The child must decide whom to believe. <break time="0.8s" /> In general, from an early age children would choose to believe a person they have a strong relationship with over a stranger. <break time="0.8s" /> At age three, they would still do this even if the familiar person has a history of having given names to objects that the child recognized to be wrong. <break time="0.8s" /> By age five, though, they will give more credence to a relative stranger who has some history of having been accurate than to a familiar person with a record of inaccuracy. <break time="0.8s" /> What happens if there are two strangers to choose between with similar records of accuracy. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the stranger who comes from the same cultural group as the child, as determined by accent, for example, is the one believed. <break time="0.8s" /> Experiments have also been done on adults, who, like children, use information about the source of theories to decide whether to adopt them. <break time="0.8s" /> We tend to follow opinion leaders, people in authority and those whose beliefs we share. <break time="0.8s" /> Similar experiments show that among chimpanzees, those with higher status are trusted more. <break time="0.8s" /> We all need ways of deciding whom to believe. <break time="0.8s" /> Evolution has provided us and other species a start.

In technological design. <break time="0.8s" /> An aspiration towards seamlessness aims to make. <break time="0.8s" /> The technological experience for humans. <break time="0.8s" /> Blend seamlessly into our everyday lives. <break time="0.8s" /> Essentially, this aspiration aims towards experiences. <break time="0.8s" /> Where people are no longer aware of the technology, the interface or the differences. <break time="0.8s" /> Between human technology and human human interaction. <break time="0.8s" /> Considering the metaphor of seams in clothing. <break time="0.8s" /> We can say that we aspire to seamless aesthetics. <break time="0.8s" /> By stitching the seams closely, pressing them flat. <break time="0.8s" /> And making sure they are hidden on the inside. <break time="0.8s" /> So that we wear clothing rather than pieces of fabric. <break time="0.8s" /> When designers and engineers talk about technological seamlessness. <break time="0.8s" /> They are often referring to ease of use and convenience. <break time="0.8s" /> For example, in interface design. <break time="0.8s" /> An aspiration towards seamlessness ensures. <break time="0.8s" /> The experience for the user flows. <break time="0.8s" /> And is not stressful or irritating. <break time="0.8s" /> Most of us would have had experiences. <break time="0.8s" /> Of poor interface designs or apps in workplaces. <break time="0.8s" /> That make things more complicated and irritating. <break time="0.8s" /> And have longed for more seamless interfaces. <break time="0.8s" /> Technological seamlessness can also include. <break time="0.8s" /> Less visible screens in new technologies. <break time="0.8s" /> Or virtual reality technologies with a seamless technological design. <break time="0.8s" /> The aim is to immerse the user experience. <break time="0.8s" /> Such that the visual interaction might be described. <break time="0.8s" /> As inside the screen rather than a body. <break time="0.8s" /> Interacting with a In technological design, an aspiration towards seamlessness aims to make the technological experience for humans blend seamlessly into our everyday lives. <break time="0.8s" /> Essentially, this aspiration aims towards experiences where people are no longer aware of the technology, the interface or the differences between human technology and human human interaction. <break time="0.8s" /> Considering the metaphor of seams in clothing, we can say that we aspire to seamless aesthetics by stitching the seams closely, pressing them flat and making sure they are hidden on the inside so that we wear clothing rather than pieces of fabric. <break time="0.8s" /> When designers and engineers talk about technological seamlessness, they are often referring to ease of use and convenience. <break time="0.8s" /> For example, in interface design, an aspiration towards seamlessness ensures the experience for the user flows and is not stressful or irritating. <break time="0.8s" /> Most of us would have had experiences of poor interface designs or apps in workplaces that make things more complicated and irritating, and have longed for more seamless interfaces. <break time="0.8s" /> Technological seamlessness can also include less visible screens in new technologies, or virtual reality technologies with a seamless technological design. <break time="0.8s" /> The aim is to immerse the user experience such that the visual interaction might be described as inside the screen rather than a body interacting with a digital console or object as separate entities. <break time="0.8s" /> Similarly, seamlessness in humanoid robotic design aims to make humanoids indistinguishable from a human body.
